name: Rollout reach
definition: Share of all eligible tasks that went through the release that day.
formula: release tasks ÷ all eligible tasks

name: Seen within 48 h
definition: Users who opened or acted on the task within 48 hours of getting it.
formula: tasks seen ≤48 h ÷ tasks received
question: 2 Know what happened
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Seen within 1 hour
definition: Users who opened or acted on the task within 1 hour. Early signal of whether the alert and entry point work.
formula: tasks seen ≤1 h ÷ tasks received
question: 2 Know what happened
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: User finished their part
definition: Users who did the action the release asks of them within 48 hours (for STV: marked the ticket resolved, sending it for verification).
formula: tasks with user action ≤48 h ÷ tasks received
question: 3 Know what to do
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: User finished within 4 working hours
definition: Users who did their part within 4 working hours (11:00–21:00 clock).
formula: tasks with user action ≤240 working min ÷ tasks received
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: First-attempt success
definition: Of tasks the user finished, the share accepted first time with no failure or retry.
formula: passed first time ÷ tasks the user finished
question: 3 Know what to do
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Failure / reopen rate
definition: Tasks sent back to the user because the system check failed.
formula: tasks reopened ÷ tasks received
question: 3 Know what to do
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Needed help
definition: Tasks where the user called the helpline about the task or app before it finished.
formula: tasks with a helpline call ÷ tasks received
question: 5 Recover and get help
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Helpline calls per 1,000 users
definition: Task or app helpline calls within 24 hours of reaching the key step, per 1,000 users who reached it.
formula: calls ÷ users reaching the step × 1,000
question: 5 Recover and get help
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Completed unaided
definition: Tasks completed within 48 hours with no helpline call. North star: at least 90% by Day 30.
formula: completed with no help ÷ tasks received
question: 6 Learn to finish alone
target_by: Manager's ask: ≥90% by Day 30

name: Completed
definition: Tasks completed within 48 hours, with or without help.
formula: completed ≤48 h ÷ tasks received
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Completed after getting help
definition: Of tasks where the user called the helpline, the share completed after the call.
formula: completed after the call ÷ tasks with a call
question: 5 Recover and get help
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Users at ≥90% unaided
definition: Users whose tasks that day were at least 90% completed unaided. Adoption at the user level, not the task level.
formula: users with ≥90% unaided ÷ users with a task
question: 6 Learn to finish alone
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Closed as time over
definition: Tasks closed because time ran out, not because they were done.
formula: time-over closes ÷ tasks received
question: 4 Know what Wiom will do next
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Closed within 24 hours
definition: Tasks fully closed within 24 hours of creation. For STV the 24 h verification hold makes this near zero by design.
formula: closed ≤24 h ÷ tasks received

name: Closed within 4 working hours
definition: Tasks fully closed within the 4-hour customer promise. For STV closure waits on the 24 h hold, so compare 'User finished within 4 working hours' instead.
formula: closed ≤240 working min ÷ tasks received

name: Repeat complaint within 7 days
definition: Closed tasks followed by a new complaint on the same connection within 7 days. Shows whether completed really means fixed.
formula: closed tasks with a new complaint ≤7 d ÷ closed tasks
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Saw the launch explainer
definition: CSPs with a ticket that day who had already seen the release's in-app explainer.
formula: CSPs who saw the explainer ÷ CSPs with a ticket
question: 1 Understand the change
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Understood the change
definition: Of CSPs who answered the explainer's check question, the share who got it right first time.
formula: right first time ÷ CSPs who answered
question: 1 Understand the change
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Did it themselves in the app
definition: Of tasks the CSP side finished, the share finished with the CSP's own tap in the app (not by an agent or the system).
formula: finished by an in-app tap ÷ tasks finished by the CSP side
question: 3 Know what to do
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Finished in one sitting
definition: Tasks finished within 30 minutes of the CSP first opening them. Low values mean the CSP had to leave and come back, often because the next step was unclear.
formula: finished ≤30 min after first open ÷ tasks opened and finished
question: 3 Know what to do
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Came back to check while waiting
definition: Tasks the CSP reopened while Wiom was verifying them. High values mean the CSP isn't sure what Wiom will do next or when.
formula: tasks reopened during verification ÷ tasks sent for verification
question: 4 Know what Wiom will do next
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Recovered after a failed check
definition: Of tasks sent back after a failed check, the share the CSP fixed and got closed.
formula: failed tasks later closed resolved ÷ failed tasks
question: 5 Recover and get help
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Unaided on first 3 tasks
definition: Completed unaided on a CSP's first three tasks of the new flow. Shows how well the design works for a first-timer.
formula: unaided tasks ÷ tasks, CSP's 1st–3rd
question: 6 Learn to finish alone
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Unaided once experienced
definition: Completed unaided from a CSP's 4th task of the new flow onwards. The gap to first-timers shows how much CSPs learn by doing.
formula: unaided tasks ÷ tasks, CSP's 4th onwards
question: 6 Learn to finish alone
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: False closes that reached the customer (72 h)
definition: Tickets the CSP side closed as resolved where the customer raised a new complaint on the same connection within 72 hours. The customer was told it was fixed when it wasn't.
formula: closed as resolved with a new complaint ≤72 h ÷ closed as resolved
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: False closes that reached the customer (24 h)
definition: Closed as resolved, then a new complaint on the same connection within 24 hours: almost certainly not fixed.
formula: closed as resolved with a new complaint ≤24 h ÷ closed as resolved
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: False closes that reached the customer (7 days)
definition: Closed as resolved, then a new complaint on the same connection within 7 days.
formula: closed as resolved with a new complaint ≤7 d ÷ closed as resolved
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: All false 'resolved' claims
definition: Every time the CSP side said a ticket was resolved and it wasn't: caught by the customer check, or reached the customer within 72 hours. Shows whether CSPs make fewer false claims, not just whether we catch them.
formula: claims caught + claims leaked ≤72 h ÷ all claims of resolved
question: 3 Know what to do
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: False claims caught before the customer
definition: Claims of resolved that the customer check rejected during the 24 h hold (customer said not fixed, or complained again), so the ticket went back to the CSP.
formula: claims rejected by the customer check ÷ claims of resolved
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Customer said not fixed
definition: Claims rejected because the customer, when asked, said the issue was not fixed.
formula: customer said no ÷ claims of resolved

name: Customer complained again during the hold
definition: Claims rejected because the customer complained again during the 24 h verification hold.
formula: customer complained again ÷ claims of resolved

name: False claims on first 3 tickets
definition: All false claims (caught or leaked ≤72 h) on a CSP's first three tickets of the flow.
formula: false claims ÷ claims, CSP's 1st–3rd ticket
question: 6 Learn to finish alone
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: False claims once experienced
definition: All false claims on a CSP's 4th ticket onwards. Lower than first-timers means CSPs learn not to claim falsely.
formula: false claims ÷ claims, CSP's 4th ticket onwards
question: 6 Learn to finish alone
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Marked resolved while the internet was down
definition: The CSP marked the ticket resolved but Wiom's internet check (CVS) saw no working internet by the end of the 30-minute initial check. The false close this release exists to stop. Old flow: closes where CVS said down.
formula: marks with no positive internet verdict ≤30 min ÷ resolved marks
question: 3 Know what to do
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Customer asked if it's fixed
definition: Resolved marks where the customer got the 'is your internet working?' message. Guardrail G3: every customer must be asked.
formula: marks with the first message sent ÷ resolved marks
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Customer answered
definition: Of customers asked, the share who said yes or reopened it, instead of staying silent.
formula: customer yes or reopen ÷ customers asked, finished
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Rated after saying yes
definition: Of customers who confirmed the fix, the share who went on to rate.
formula: rated ÷ customer confirmed

name: Closed: customer confirmed
definition: Verification ended with the customer saying yes, it works.
formula: customer confirmed ÷ verifications closed
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Closed: internet working, no reply
definition: Verification ended by the timer: the internet check was positive but the customer never replied.
formula: internet working, no reply ÷ verifications closed

name: Closed: not verified
definition: Verification ended by the timer with no positive internet check and no reply. Closed without proof the internet works.
formula: not verified ÷ verifications closed
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Closed by the Wiom CX team
definition: A Wiom CX agent closed the ticket in Kapture during verification.
formula: closed by Wiom CX ÷ verifications closed
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Clear decision within 24 h
definition: Bookings the CSP accepted or declined within 24 hours of the booking reaching them. The opposite is a booking left hanging.
formula: accepted or declined ≤24 h ÷ bookings reached
question: 3 Know what to do
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Timed out with no decision
definition: Bookings taken back from the CSP because the hold window ran out with no accept and no decline.
formula: timed out unaccepted ÷ bookings reached
question: 2 Know what happened
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Declined
definition: Bookings the CSP declined, with a reason.
formula: declined ÷ bookings reached

name: Accepted
definition: Bookings the CSP accepted. On the old flow, assigning a technician is the acceptance.
formula: accepted ÷ bookings reached
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Technician assigned within 24 h
definition: Bookings with a technician assigned within 24 hours of reaching the CSP.
formula: technician assigned ≤24 h ÷ bookings reached
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Accepted but no technician in 24 h
definition: Of bookings accepted within 24 hours, the share still without a technician 24 hours after reaching the CSP: a yes with no follow-through.
formula: accepted, no technician by 24 h ÷ accepted ≤24 h
question: 3 Know what to do
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Installed within 14 days
definition: Bookings that reached the CSP and were installed within 14 days.
formula: installed ≤14 d ÷ bookings reached
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Accepted bookings installed
definition: Of bookings the CSP accepted, the share installed: did a yes turn into a connection?
formula: installed ÷ accepted
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Accepted, then install failed
definition: Of bookings the CSP accepted, the share where the installation was reported failed.
formula: install reported failed ÷ accepted
target_by: Proposed by the adoption team, not agreed

name: Confirmed on the consent sheet
definition: Of consent sheets opened, the share where the CSP went on to accept the booking.
formula: accepted after the sheet ÷ consent sheets opened
question: 1 Understand the change

name: Backed out of the consent sheet
definition: Of consent sheets opened, the share the CSP closed without accepting. Some back-out is the point: an informed no.
formula: sheets closed without accepting ÷ consent sheets opened
question: 1 Understand the change

name: Reopened within 30 days (impact)
definition: Closed as resolved, then a new complaint on the same connection within 30 days. The release's impact metric in the design spec.
formula: closed as resolved with a new complaint ≤30 d ÷ closed as resolved

name: Resolved within the CSP's TAT
definition: Complaints resolved within the CSP's TAT (Support Resolution). Design-spec guardrail: must not get worse.
formula: within TAT ÷ complaints with a TAT result

name: Closed only after the CSP's mark (G2)
definition: Closed complaints that had a Resolved mark first, or were closed by Wiom CX (the one allowed exception).
formula: closed with a mark or by CX ÷ closed

name: Every closure has a recorded cause (G6)
definition: Closed complaints with a closure reason recorded.
formula: closed with a reason ÷ closed

name: Backed out of the confirm sheet
definition: The CSP opened 'start verification?' and did not mark the ticket resolved within 30 minutes.
formula: sheets with no resolved mark ≤30 min ÷ sheets opened
question: 3 Know what to do

name: Resolved mark failed or offline
definition: The CSP tapped to mark resolved but the mark did not reach Wiom (failure or offline).
formula: failed marks ÷ marks attempted
question: 3 Know what to do

name: Opened within 1 h of a reopen
definition: After a ticket was reopened to the CSP, the CSP opened it in the app within 1 hour.
formula: reopens opened ≤1 h ÷ reopens
question: 5 Recover and get help

name: Reopened outside working hours
definition: Reopens that landed outside 11:00–21:00, when the CSP's clock is paused until morning.
formula: night reopens ÷ reopens

name: Accepted within 1 h
definition: Bookings accepted within 1 hour of reaching the CSP. Stands in for the spec's median time to accept.
formula: accepted ≤1 h ÷ bookings reached

name: Technician within 1 h of accepting
definition: Of accepted bookings, the share with a technician assigned within 1 hour of accepting. Stands in for the spec's median time from accept to assign.
formula: assigned ≤1 h after accept ÷ accepted
question: 3 Know what to do

name: Accepts that went through the consent sheet (G1)
definition: Accepted bookings at consent CSPs where the consent sheet was opened for that booking first.
formula: accepts with a consent sheet ÷ accepts
